findings: Buys: over the five trading days from the fill, the stocks it bought beat SPY by 0.43% on average (23 buys, 57% of them ahead of SPY; t = 0.7, within noise).
Sells: over the five trading days from the fill, the stocks it sold beat SPY by 0.97%, so selling gave that up (42 sells; t = -1.8, within noise).
Decision IC: on the 12 days it traded, what it bought ranked against what it sold and left alone by a mean rank IC of -0.020 with the next five days' returns (IC IR -0.17, t = -0.6, within noise).
Holdings IC: the weights it held after each of 50 decision days had a mean rank IC of -0.011 with the next five days' returns (t = -0.5, within noise).
Factor exposures: market 0.60 (t 23.1), size -0.18 (t -5.0), growth 0.02 (t 0.2), momentum 0.01 (t 0.2); together they explain 91% of the daily variation (R²).
Of the +13.5% a year it earned over T-bills (arithmetic mean): market +12.7%, size -0.9%, growth +0.4%, momentum +0.1%; the alpha left is +1.1% a year (t = 0.2, within noise).
Verdict: most of the return is factor exposure (+12.4% a year, market above all); the alpha left is not significant.
P&L: +$12,490 in all, +$12,404 from 14 positions and +$86 of interest on idle cash.
By holding period: 61+ days made the most (+$13,215, 12 positions); 11-20 days the least (-$970, 1 position).
By sector: Health Care made the most (+$5,240, 3 positions); Energy the least (-$970, 1 position).
By stock: MSFT made the most (+$2,716, 1 position); CVX the least (-$970, 1 position).
By market regime of the previous close: risk-on 26 days -2.0% (SPY -4.3%); uncertain 142 days +7.8% (SPY +14.2%); risk-off 85 days +6.5% (SPY +7.2%).
News: 2 positions opened on news made +$1,976, the other 12 +$10,428; 1 positions closed on news made +$159; over the five days from the fill, news-triggered buys beat SPY by 3.29% (t 10.1).

Concentration: the profit is spread out; the best two positions made 44% of the positions' net P&L, the best being MSFT bought 2020-01-03 and still open at the end, +$2,716. Had the best position made nothing, the run would have returned +9.8% instead of +12.5%.
